title: The three loops and one if
summary: Branch with a real bool, then repeat work three different ways.

blocks.html: if takes a condition, then a block in braces that runs when the condition is true. Note there are no parentheses around the condition. Add else if to ask the next question, and a final else to catch everything that is left. The conditions are checked top to bottom and the first true one wins.

blocks.title: one chain, three answers
a number is not a condition

blocks.html:
Rust has no truthiness. A condition must be a real bool, so this fails with error[E0308]: mismatched types and the note expected bool, found integer. Nothing is converted for you: neither zero, nor an empty list, nor a non-null pointer counts as false.

Write the comparison you mean: if x != 0. The extra characters buy the reader certainty about what is being tested.

An if is an expression, so it can produce a value. Both branches must then have the same type, and the whole thing can sit on the right of a let. This replaces the ternary operator you may know from other languages. (For the parity test below, % is the remainder after division, so n % 2 is zero exactly when n is even.)

blocks.title: if as a value

blocks.html: loop repeats a block forever until something stops it. break ends the loop immediately. And because a loop is an expression, break may carry a value out with it: break n; ends the loop and makes n the value of the whole loop.

blocks.title: loop that hands back an answer

blocks.html:
while repeats its block while a condition stays true, rechecking before every pass. for is the one to reach for most days: it walks a range or an array and stops on its own. A range with two dots, 1..5, stops before the last number; three dots and an equals sign, 1..=5, includes it. continue skips the rest of the current pass and jumps to the next one, and it only affects the loop it sits in.

Which to choose: for when there is a range or an array to walk, while when a condition decides when to stop, and loop when neither fits and you will break out yourself.

blocks.title: for over an array, continue, and a loop inside a loop

quiz.q: How many lines does this print? for n in 1..4 { println!("{n}"); }
quiz.why: 1..4 stops before 4, so the values are 1, 2 and 3. The inclusive form 1..=4 would print four lines.

quiz.q: Which condition compiles inside an if?
quiz.why: The condition must be a bool, and only a comparison produces one. A bare integer gives expected bool, found integer, and = is assignment rather than comparison.

quiz.q: A loop can hand a value out. What does let x = loop { break 7; }; bind x to?
quiz.why: A loop is an expression, and break can carry a value out of it. That value becomes the value of the loop, so x is 7.

exercise.brief: Using a for loop over 1..=10, add up only the even numbers into sum, then print the total.
exercise.hint: Inside the loop, if n % 2 != 0 { continue; } jumps straight to the next number, so the line after it runs only for even n.
